meta.title: My Bag for Monday
meta.textType: story: two lists and one bag

paragraphs: On Friday, May fourteenth, in the evening, Lily packed her bag for the new school. Her first day was on Monday. On her bedroom floor lay a folded white shirt, a dark blue skirt, and a gray hoodie. A water bottle and two pens lay beside them. The school bag stood open next to the clothes, and Pip sat in it with his red ball. Tom stood in the doorway and watched. Earlier, Mom put the new uniform on the floor. "The uniform has already been washed in the washing machine," she told Lily. "It has just been taken in from the garden," she added. "A uniform is not about fashion," said Mom, and then she went back to the kitchen.

Tom came into the room and gave Lily a paper. "This is my list for M one," he said. The list had a hoodie, a water bottle, two pens, and a slim notebook. "Why do I need a hoodie?" asked Lily. "The rooms are cold, so take a hoodie," said Tom. Then the doorbell rang, and Tom ran downstairs. He came back with a second paper from Sam. Sam's list had lunch money for the cafeteria, a plain hoodie, a water bottle, and two pens. "Sam says that a plain hoodie is allowed," said Tom. Lily put the two lists side by side on the floor.

Next, Lily looked at her laptop on the desk. An email from her pen pal Grace was on the screen. "Dear Lily, here is my advice for Monday." "First, breathe slowly." "Then, smile at one person." "Good luck!" "Best wishes, Grace."

Pip jumped out of the bag with his red ball. "What is different, and what is the same?" asked Lily. "Both lists have a hoodie, a water bottle, and two pens," said Tom. "Sam has lunch money, and I have a notebook." Lily took a pencil and wrote her own list. First, she wrote the hoodie, the water bottle, and three pens, because one extra pen is useful. Next, she added a slim notebook and lunch money for her wallet. Then she added an umbrella, because rain may come in the afternoon. Finally, she put a library card in the front pocket of the bag. The gray hoodie was soft and comfortable, so she put it on top. The bag stayed tidy, and Lily checked it three times.
"You will be fine," Tom told her. "I know," said Lily, and she zipped the bag. Then she breathed slowly. She smiled at Tom, and Pip dropped the red ball beside the bag.
